title: The Guide to Fixing a Broken People

sense.text:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning”: whatever was written before time was written for us to take it and learn from it. This class is the guide to fixing a broken people, so we have to go back and read the scriptures to understand how to fix us. The US government is not going to fix us. The food stamp welfare office, the Section 8 vouchers, voting, the Christian church, Islam: none of it is going to fix us. If it was going to fix us it would have fixed us already, and it ain’t fixed us.

The Christian church doesn’t teach what was written before time. They say it is done away with: don’t go to the Old Testament, it’s all about Jesus now. That is why people are lost and at the bottom of society; the Christian church has failed the black community. They do the dancing and the good singing. A pastor who knows how to sing, and can do a little two-step with it, will have a bigger congregation than the old pastor sitting in the Baptist church with his big glasses on having Easter egg hunts.

“That we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Through patience: we are waiting on the Messiah to return, and waiting patiently. Through comfort: whatever you are going through, the scriptures are here to comfort us. The things written before time will give you comfort.

We have to go back to the days of old to understand how to fix a broken people. This is King David: “Give ear, O my people”. My people are the children of Israel, and that is another problem that is not being taught in the world: who the children of Israel are today. People misinterpret the Bible because they don’t understand who the characters in the Bible are today. We do not understand that we are the people of the Bible.

“To my law”: to his law, not the laws of the United States. A lot of the laws of the United States are based off God’s laws, but you have to give ear to the Bible first. “Incline your ears to the words of my mouth”: open your ears up. The words of his mouth are the Bible.

“I will open my mouth in a parable”: the Most High speaks in parables because everybody is not going to be able to understand the Bible. He didn’t want everybody to understand it; he didn’t want the heathen to understand it.

“I will utter dark sayings of old”: everybody is not going to understand it. It’s 2023 and our people still do not understand the dark sayings of old, and that is why we could not fix our community. Everybody is trying to fix it their own way, but today we are giving the guide to fixing a broken people.

precepts.why:
The words of his mouth are the Bible. “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read”: this is the only way we are going to fix the problem of us being a broken people. The Bible is the guide. It ain’t the YMCA, the community center, the community activists, or all the different programs they set up in the community to keep us lost.

A lot of black people don’t understand the importance of reading the Bible. We love to go to church and see our pastor mimic the Bible the way our forefathers did in slavery. Pay attention when you go to church: they read one scripture and close the book. Back in the slavery days they didn’t know how to read; all they knew was four or five words, ‘for God so loved the world’, and then they’d close the book, get up and start whooping and hollering. That is where they learned it. They are mad at us because we open the Bible, actually read it, and go into it to find the problem and fix the problem. That is why they don’t like us.

“No one of these shall fail”: the prophecies, which this class goes through, are not going to fail.

“None shall want her mate”: you can’t mate the Bible with nothing else. That is another thing people try to do to fix the problems in the black community: put the Bible with the Quran, with the Kabbalah, with the 42 laws and all that. You can’t even mate the Bible with Christianity, because Christianity is not in the Bible, and that is why our communities are not being fixed. “For my mouth it hath commanded”.

Dark sayings of old, which everybody is not going to understand. “If a man desire much experience, she knoweth things of old”: she is wisdom, and she knows things of old. That is where experience comes from, from what has been done in the past. So you have to read the past to understand what is going on now, “and conjectureth aright what is to come”.

“She knoweth the subtilties of speeches”: wisdom knows the trickery of people who give speeches, “and can expound dark sentences”, the same dark sayings of old in Psalm 78. “She foreseeth signs and wonders, and the events of seasons and times.”

“Therefore I purposed to take her to me to live with me, knowing that she would be a counsellor of good things, and a comfort in cares and grief.” “For her sake I shall have estimation among the multitude, and honour with the elders, though I be young.”

Don’t ever let nobody tell you the Old Testament is done away with, that we don’t have to live by it, that we don’t even have to read it. That is what the Christian church does, and that is why we are lost.

“Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee”. The scripture says to remember the days of old, so you have to go back in the scriptures and remember the things that were written aforetime, because they were written for our learning. We first have to know who our forefathers are to understand what is being written.

sense.text:
Getting into the guide to fixing a broken people: first we have to remember and know that we are the children of Israel, that the Bible pertains to us. It belongs to us, it was written for us, and it was written by us, ordained by the Most High.

“The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be”: you have to understand the past. “And that which is done is that which shall be done”: what was done in the past is being done right now. “And there is no new thing under the sun.” It is like we are in another time zone, another time, but we are living the scriptures again in 2023.

“Is there any thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new?” As a black people we like to say this is new: us being shot down and beat down in the street, us being killed, the black man not being in the home, the black woman being ratchet and being thought of that way. Those are just new words; it is not new. This is not the first time we have fallen so bad and become an astonishment. In every captivity we have been in, in the scriptures, Deuteronomy 28 has come to pass, and we have become an astonishment, a proverb and a byword. “It hath been already of old time, which was before us.”

“There is no remembrance of former things”: we can’t remember those former things because we came back through the birth canal of our mother into this world. “Neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.”

The class reads a lot in the Old Testament today about Babylon and Persia and the different captivities we were in. What we went through in Babylon is synonymous with what we are going through right now in Babylon the great, which is America. We went through this thousands of years ago.

“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”. “Which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt”. It is called Sodom because America is the first place to legalize same-sex marriage. They are teaching it in the schools; they have transgender people teaching their children and saying it’s okay, and God said it’s not okay. It is called Egypt because the children of Israel were brought here in bulk to serve our enemies; we are back in captivity, we are back in Egypt.

You are not going to learn this in the Christian church. That is why we tell people to come out of it. There you learn how to celebrate Easter, Christmas, Dr. King Day; some just celebrated Groundhog Day. On the news in the break room at work: Esau, the damn white man with his hat on, holding a damn rodent in his hand, a groundhog that looks like a beaver, putting it on the stage and reading a letter saying the groundhog didn’t see his shadow so it will be six more weeks of winter, and everybody goes whoa. Esau is a damn devil, and black people are right there with it; they had us believing in Groundhog Day when we were kids. These people are the damn devil, and we have to come out of this stuff.

precepts.why:
That great city is a future-tense prophecy of America. “And the woman which thou sawest is that great city, which reigneth over the kings of the earth.” What city reigns over all the kings of the earth? America. They can’t do nothing without America’s consent. If somebody is building a bomb, or selling drugs or opium somewhere, the white man is going to come holler at them; they have to check in with the white man and can’t just do what they want to do.

So the woman is that great city that reigns over the kings of the earth, America, Babylon the great. It is future prophecy, and that is how you know the Bible is real, though a lot of people do not understand it.

sense.text:
To fix a broken people you have to know how the people got broken. To fix anything you have to know where it is broken and how it broke.

“See, I have set before thee this day life and good”: the Lord set before the children of Israel way back then life and good, things everybody wants. “And death and evil”: he set two things. People don’t understand that the Lord does all these things. When people die, whoever it is, the Lord done it. The Christian church doesn’t teach that; they say the devil did this, the devil did that. When someone is sick you pray that the Lord’s will be done, and at the end of the day the Lord’s will is going to be done.

The evil and the dying we are seeing amongst our people, the Lord set that before us, just like the good things: people waking up, coming out of the Christian church, out of Islam, out of all the different philosophies, and coming back to their true nationality as the Israelites. God set that up. We didn’t set it up; he is just using us as vessels to wake the people up. It was planned way before we were born, before America was established. So to the haters out there: don’t hate us, hate God, because everything being done is of the Lord.

God put life and good and death and evil in front of us, “In that I command thee this day to love the Lord thy God”.

“To walk in his ways”: to walk in the commandments, the same commandments they teach are done away with, “and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply”: live and multiply, not die and keep dying. We have to keep God’s commandments if we want to live and keep multiplying.

“And the Lord thy God shall bless thee in the land whither thou goest to possess it”: when we do that, the Most High will bless us wherever we go. If we start keeping the commandments, he will start to bless us. This is what is not being understood: who we are and who God is talking to. They say you don’t have to read this, it doesn’t pertain to you. Their eyes are shut and their ears are stopped up; they don’t understand that we are the children of Israel and God is speaking directly to us about us. So they keep complaining and keep marching for justice and peace.

“But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear”: here he gives you the ultimatum. If you become hardheaded and stiffnecked, turn your mind away from the scriptures and don’t want to hear the Bible, like the majority of you Negroes do, “but shalt be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them”.

One god we learned to worship was white Jesus. They love to say it doesn’t matter what color Jesus is, but if it doesn’t matter why did they paint him white? It only doesn’t matter when we say he looked like us, and when we tell the people he is coming back to save us. Black people feel everybody has to be included in the salvation of Jesus Christ. They really think God is coming back to save the Jewish people that own everything, so they can keep their PornHub up, keep their social media deteriorating the minds of our youth, keep pushing rap music that destroys our community, and have more Beyoncé concerts with thousand-dollar tickets. The Lord has to destroy these people, and if Beyoncé doesn’t repent he is going to destroy her. They hate us because we tell the truth.

A preacher with a Jheri curl put out a video, mad that people are leaving the Christian church: brothers and sisters who used to be witnesses for the Lord Jesus Christ, who have seen the power of the Holy Ghost, have left the church for the Black Hebrew Israelites. He says we draw people away by telling them they serve a white Jesus. When we say that, we are telling them they are following the doctrine of Christianity, and Christianity was set up with white Jesus. He says we claim to be the true descendants of the tribes of Israel; then if we are not the true descendants of the tribes of Israel, who are we? These Christian churches cannot prove who we are in the Bible. He says Jesus Christ is the savior of all mankind; black people all want to save mankind. He says we identify with the curses of Deuteronomy 28, fulfilled at the transatlantic slave trade, but that white Anglo-Saxons also say they are the lost tribes of Israel. You have to go in the scriptures and see whether those white Anglo-Saxons are telling the truth.

And the power of the Holy Ghost he is talking about: the videos of church folk jumping and dancing, a woman with a damn fish tank on top of her head, mama doing the gangster walk, the bankhead bounce and the Memphis juke. All the dances come out of the Christian church. This garbage is why we are dying in the streets. That is not the power of the Holy Ghost; that is demonic worship, that is just having rhythm. That is what we just saw: we were drawn away and worshipped other gods, and they learned that from Christianity. Nowhere in the Bible did the Holy Ghost fall on people and they danced. When the Holy Ghost fell on people they spoke in different tongues, meaning different languages. We have to come out of these Christian churches; it is time for these pastors to step down if they want to fix the broken people.

“I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish”: no ifs, ands or buts. If we serve other gods we will surely perish, “and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land”: we are not going to live long.

“I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing”. Our people choose death and curses; they don’t like to choose life. “Therefore choose life”: he told us what to choose, and keeping the commandments is choosing life.

We can’t just do what we want to do on this earth. It is time for our people to wake up, and it is our duty to hit the streets and wake them up. But the people don’t want us out there. When the purple and gold hit the block, the drug dealers and some in the community hate to see us come and love to see us leave; sometimes they clap when we leave, not understanding we are there to try to fix their problems. They don’t understand they are sick.

“That thou mayest love the Lord thy God”: to love God means keeping his commandments; whatever God says do, we are going to do it. “And that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life”: the Lord is our life, our life is in his hands, “and the length of thy days: that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.”

precepts.why:
What does it mean to love God? People think they are going to give the Lord chocolate and teddy bears on Valentine’s Day and give him a hug. That is not the love of God, and God don’t give a damn about you trying to hug him; he didn’t make your arms long enough.

“For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments”. God doesn’t care what you say; you have to obey the things he commanded us to do. Stop teaching that the commandments are done away with. This is the guide to fixing a broken people: we have to come back to God’s law, statutes and commandments.

Y’all can’t just keep complaining that the young ones keep shooting up one another, that the girls are twerking and coming in the house pregnant, that they are killing one another. What are you going to do about it? You are so caught up in your ways that you don’t want to change yourself, so you are left complaining. What happened in Memphis will be gone from the news once the Super Bowl comes on, the way you forgot George Floyd, Sean Bell and Tamir Rice. These things are set up to be pacifiers to black people. When things happen, God is using them as a sign to wake us up. It is not only that white people hate us: black devils hate each other too. The Lord uses the death and evil to prove a point and wake us up.

“And his commandments are not grievous.” They are not hard to do; y’all just hate to do them. Y’all want to keep the 12 days of Christmas and the Easter egg hunt. It ain’t hard to stop eating pork. People justify eating the chitlins, the guts, every part of the pig, the toenails, the eyeballs. Talking to brothers about pork is like being in a drug anonymous program: do not relapse. The hog was the nastiest stuff they ever gave us, and we made it a delicacy with Louisiana hot sauce on it. Get rid of the pork.

Black people won’t obey the laws of God; they want to do their own thing. They won’t stop eating pork, shrimp, crab and lobster. The women want everybody to see them in their nasty pants and their black ass butt cheeks; that is how they feel they get attention. They don’t want to change; they just like to complain.

Choose life by keeping the commandments. “Keep my commandments, and live”: this is how you live and how you get life, by keeping the Lord’s commandments.

He gave you dietary laws, ceremonial laws, civil laws and moral laws to live by. The only law you don’t have to keep is the sacrificial law; that is what Christ died for. This is what we keep trying to tell people, and they come up against us and hate us.

sense.text:
These are basic scriptures everybody should know, good ones to pull out when you are out teaching, because our people hate to see us coming.

“And go, get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people”: the people who were enslaved, who went through the transatlantic slave trade or the sub-Saharan slave trade. “And speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God”: we don’t come out there with our own words. We always have a Bible when we go out and teach. The pastor comes up to us with nothing in his hand, not even the app open on his phone; we have the scriptures, the Bible open.

“Whether they will hear”: whether you want to hear it, “or whether they will forbear”: whether you don’t want to hear it.

This goes on all the time: people in the community hate us for trying to fix the community. At a rally in Buffalo, New York, a black woman went to the police on us: we want them gone, they come down here to stir up this mess, they are telling us to hate white people. She was trying to get the police to stop us exercising our freedom of speech. We don’t tell nobody to hate white people. We may say God said he loved Jacob and hated Esau, but nobody in purple and gold teaches that you have to hate white people to get into the kingdom; that is a damn lie. She said don’t tell me something from 1300 years ago, but the Bible says to remember the days of old. How is she at a protest trying to fix the problem when she doesn’t even want to look into the days of old? And it is always the black woman with the bullhorn, trying to lead instead of letting the men of God lead. She said she puts her pants on just like they do; that lets you know she is destroyed. We pray these sisters repent and wake up and understand that what we are doing is the right thing. She said by the way we stand we are not with the community; so how we stand, not what we say, decides whether we are with the community.

Then at camp in Nashville a young woman jumped out of a car at the gas station where we were teaching, waving a Glock with an extended clip at the people in another car. The brother holding post saw the gun and called eyes up. The first thing was to spring into action and de-escalate with the word of God, because all she had to do was squeeze the trigger and somebody would lose their life: sister, think about your family, you have kids, don’t throw your life away for nothing, do not hate your brothers and sisters in your heart, God loves you. She acted like she wasn’t listening, but she heard the word of God. The man with her was just going to let it go down, ready to drive off and become an accessory and throw his life away too, until he was told to break it up. Then he had something to say: y’all stay in y’all lane. That is our lane: we are out there teaching, and it is our lane to protect the community with the word of God. We are not going to jump in and break them up; we let judgment be rendered on whoever God wants to render it on, but we use the word of God to calm it down. They ended up talking it out and nobody got shot or killed. We potentially stopped a murder, and still black women, pastors and black men say they don’t want us out there.

Our presence is needed. We can’t be in all places at all times, but we are going to be wherever the Lord needs us to be. This is the guide to fixing the broken people: we have to hit the streets and get boots on the ground. If you are just an internet prophet or social media prophet in our comments telling us how you would do it, typing two or three paragraphs nobody sees, be ashamed of yourself. Throw your keyboard away and get out on the streets with us on the front line, where the gunfire is. All that profound knowledge, and you ain’t teaching nobody. Be quiet, sit back and enjoy the ride, and if you don’t repent, enjoy the fire when it comes.

These are well-known scriptures. “But this is a people robbed and spoiled”: the people that have been robbed and spoiled are the Israelites, us, our families.

“They are all of them snared in holes”: a snare is a trap, a catch, a bag net. We have been entrapped. What are these traps? Religion: the people jumping around on the TV screen talking about they got the Holy Ghost, the prosperity gospel preaching they put up on TikTok, looking like they saying some profound knowledge, and it’s stupid. Look at this nasty woman twerking at church: there’s a snare in the damn hole. It got her in the strip club spirit, throwing that ass in church. That’s why we tell y’all to come out the Christian church; we got to come out these Christian churches.

Look at these little boy monsters: these games and this rap music are snares in the hole. They hope one day to get rich, hope one day the Jewish man is gonna get them ten thousand dollars a piece so they get them a chain and be broke again. He ain’t got no haircut, his pants sagging, he ain’t got no sense to put no belt on, and they all smoking weed. This is a broken people. We got to stop this somewhere, man; we got to fix our broken people. This is why it’s important for us to hit the street and put boots on the ground, why it’s important for the editing team to keep pushing videos out on social media: the Lord is using you to push this truth.

“And they are hid in prison houses”: our people are hid in prison houses. How do we fix this? “They are for a prey, and none delivereth”: they fall prey. Who are the hunters? Right now the so-called government, the white man, even our own people as we’ve seen them in Memphis. The wicked are the hunters and we the prey. You can’t even put no color on it no more; the scripture says it’s the wicked, and the wicked gonna be his sword.

“For a spoil, and none saith, Restore”: nobody’s saying restore these people. Nobody’s saying let’s get to the root of the problem: how did they end up over here, who brought them over here, and why did he do it? It’s like looking at a tree: you’re looking at the bad fruit on the tree, but not at why the fruit ended up dying on the tree like that, whether the soil is bad, the roots, the seed. You’re just looking at the fruit, and the fruit is Christianity, politics, all these things we’re trying to use to fix our problems.
“Who among you will give ear to this?” Who among us are going to get into this? “Who will hearken and hear for the time to come?”

“Who gave Jacob for a spoil, and Israel to the robbers? did not the Lord”: not the devil. The Lord done that, because we disobeyed. This is the guide to fixing our problems: we got to first understand God put us in this situation, because we disobeyed him, so we put ourselves in this situation. People say we always blaming the white man. We don’t blame the white man; we just saying the white man is the Lord’s sword, carrying out certain things, and we use the white man or the government or anybody else to show that our people are in these conditions. These are the people carrying out God’s plan and his judgments upon us.

“He against whom we have sinned”: it’s telling you what happened. We sinned against God; we broke God’s laws, statutes and his commandments. We pissed God off, we broke his law, he got mad.

“For they would not walk in his ways”: we want to do our own thing. We’ve been a disobedient people; just like now we complain, but we would not do what God commands us to do. They say get that Bible out of here, we don’t want them here. “Neither were they obedient unto his law”: just like today our people do not want to keep God’s laws. It’s the Lord’s Sabbath day, but we don’t want to remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy. We want to go to church tomorrow and dance and sing and eat some pork chops, some turnip greens and mustard greens, that ham hock, and go to grandmama house after church and watch the football game.

“Therefore he hath poured upon him the fury of his anger”: he poured upon us the fury of his anger. In 2023 we are living out the judgments of God’s anger. This is how we change the situation; a lot of people don’t want to change, they just want to complain and do the same thing. “And the strength of battle: and it hath set him on fire round about”.

precepts.why: What is sin? Somebody new could be looking on Facebook right now and not understand what sin is. “Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.” Sin is the breaking of God’s laws. This is what we must understand, and that’s what we did: “he against whom we have sinned” means we broke God’s laws, and he got angry.

Our people run into the gangs, they run into the church. “And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness”.

“And thou shalt not prosper in thy ways”: the Lord said we was not going to prosper in our ways, and he’s proven it to be true. We’re not prospering, we’re only declining.

“And thou shalt be only oppressed”: our oppressed people are broken people. “And spoiled evermore”: we spoiled, like spoiled rotten meat, like milk you can’t drink. The young women out in the projects here in Nashville with a song telling folks to come outside, all of them with them big ass eyelashes like caterpillars crawling across their face: they want you to come outside so they can fight, they want a brawl. This is happening because our people are broken; they don’t know how to love their neighbors, how to love themselves. “And no man shall save thee”.

sense.text:
People want us off the street, like we ain’t got the solutions. That’s because they under a strong delusion. They say, no, I don’t want to change; I want to keep complaining when the police gun us down and shoot us down and beat the hell out of us. They don’t want to get to the root of the problem: why the Scorpion unit was even created in the first place. East Memphis used to be the good neighborhood; with the projects gone from the Third Ward and North Memphis, all them bad ass kids that was in one place scattered out to East Memphis, drug dealing, robbing, shooting and killing. So they come up with a task force, extra aggressive on the community. Why was this unit even formed? Because of sin in our communities. If our black people loved each other and loved themselves, weren’t selling drugs to one another, if the black man was taking care of the kids and wasn’t sleeping around with every woman that’ll let him hit, we wouldn’t be going through what we’re going through. It’s sad but it’s true; we got to look at the problem and be ready to face it.

“And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion”: because they disobey God, because we disobey God, our people are under a strong delusion. When they see help on the way they don’t even understand the help that they see, because we the wrong color, we ain’t got enough money; that’s what they think. “That they should believe a lie”: the people believe lies instead of the truth.

“That they all might be damned”: that all may be snared in the hole. “Who believed not the truth”: who believe not the word of God; they all gonna be damned. “But had pleasure in unrighteousness”: these people love making them little videos telling folks to come outside, they love fighting; women twerking on the headlights at the red light. That’s spoiled meat. They destroyed, they under the delusion. Stay in the spirit; you don’t want that spoiled meat.

precepts.why:
It says the same thing: they gonna choose their delusions over the truth. That’s why a lot of people just got to get burnt up, all praises to the Most High, because the only way he’s gonna be able to reset this place is through nuclear fire.

“I also will choose their delusions”: the Most High chose the delusions we’ll be under. “And will bring their fears upon them”: the oppression we’re under, he’s going to bring that on us. “Because when I called, none did answer”: when we go out there and teach, they don’t want to answer, they don’t want to hear it. “When I spake, they did not hear”: when we go out there and speak the words of God, they keep on walking. “But they did evil”: they continue to do evil; many times when we leave camp and leave from teaching on fly missions, somebody end up dead. “And chose that in which I delighted not”: they chose sin; they chose to keep smoking weed, keep selling heroin, keep selling ass.

“Hear the word of the Lord, ye that tremble at his word”: those that fear God. “Your brethren that hated you”: our brothers that hated us, “that cast you out for my name’s sake, said, Let the Lord be glorified: but he shall appear to your joy, and they shall be ashamed”. They’re going to be ashamed for the things that they’re doing.

Our people hate the word of God. They don’t want to be fixed, but God gonna fix them whether they like it or not. They better read this guide; the guide is the Bible. They either gonna repent and turn from their wicked ways or he’s going to burn them: burn, baby, burn. He gonna burn America, and a lot of these people gonna be ashes. Like a Nintendo game, the only way to hit restart is to burn it, and it’s going to reset everything. The righteous men and women gonna be left here on earth to rule the earth and build it in righteousness under the leadership of the Most High, Christ: the men that have kept God’s commandments. We gonna have to get our slaves in order with the word of God; when the future slaves come up to camp, teach them the law too: tell them to stop killing and stealing and putting drugs in our community.

“Nevertheless they were disobedient”: our people are always disobedient. “And rebelled against thee”: they love rebelling against God. That’s why we can’t fix the community, because our people love rebellion. “And cast thy law behind their backs”: they cast the Bible behind their backs, but go to church on Sunday, on the wrong day. They hate the laws of God so much they say it’s done away with, you ain’t got to keep it.

“And slew thy prophets which testified against them to turn them to thee”: some of the people want to kill us out there; threats have been put on our lives out there on the front line, while we’re trying to fix them.

sense.text: “Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord”: destruction to these rebellious Negroes. “That take counsel, but not of me”: you go to your pastor and you take counsel, and he don’t even open the Bible. “And that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit”: not of the spirit of the Most High, “that they may add sin to sin”.

“To strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt”: they trusting America. They think America gonna fix them; that’s what it means to trust in the shadow of Egypt.

“Therefore shall the strength of Pharaoh be your shame”: the government gonna be your shame. “And the trust in the shadow of Egypt your confusion”: trusting in America and its policies, America’s religion, all these things set up, is going to be your confusion. This is why a lot of pastors are confused, a lot of preachers, ministers, and these damn women prophets; go to the clubhouse and listen to them sometime, they have no idea what they talking about.

“He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already”: if you believe not in Christ, you condemned already, “because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God”: because you have not believed in the word of God. They didn’t believe Christ was the Messiah.

“That light is come into the world”: before that they was in darkness. They were doing animal sacrifice, sinning on purpose; as long as they had two turtle doves and a bullock they thought they was cool, and they wanted to keep doing that. When Christ came on the scene, their animal sacrifices was going to be done away with; he was messing with their belief system. That’s why they did not want to accept him: they wanted to continue to walk in darkness and reject the light. It’s the same thing going on today.

“And men loved darkness rather than light”: our people love darkness and hate the light. The darkness is sin; our people love sin more than keeping the commandments, they love Satan more than they love Christ. “Because their deeds were evil”: they were sacrificing and sinning on purpose, and thought it was going to continue, because the scribes and Pharisees had got rich. They weren’t no poor people: they had all the food, all the meats, people bringing them tithes.

Just like the Christian pastors today: they know what we’re saying is true, that we’re the children of Israel and we must keep God’s laws, statutes and commandments, but they will not tell you, because once you believe in Christ you’re going to stop bringing them tithes and offerings. It’s all about money to them. Some of these damn pastors dropped out of school, didn’t go to no college, didn’t go back and get their GED; they started pimping, selling drugs, doing all type of stuff, and when they got in their 30s, 40s and 50s they started preaching. No 401K, no pension; they never really worked. So if you teaching keep God’s commandments, you taking away their livelihood, and they fighting for it. They’ll be out there homeless under the damn bridge if they don’t keep preaching and keep people in a delusional state of mind in Christianity.

“For every one that doeth evil”: that means break God’s commandments, “hateth the light”: they hate Christ, because Christ is the light. “Neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved”: lest their deeds be corrected. They like standing in darkness. They don’t like us because we shine the light on them: when everybody’s in darkness and the light walks in the room, that light gonna hit the dark people, and that’s how you able to see them. So they don’t want you in the room, period. The light shows their true colors, that he’s a liar, he’s a pimp, and they don’t want nobody to reveal who they really are.

“But he that doeth truth cometh to the light”: if you’re keeping God’s commandments, you’re gonna come to the light, you’re gonna love the light, you’re gonna understand the light. Some people like walking in darkness with night vision glasses on when you can just cut the damn light on and see everything. “That his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.”

precepts.why: What is the light that is come into the world? “For the commandment is a lamp”: the commandments of God is a lamp. “And the law is light”: the laws of God is light, and that’s Christ. So when men love darkness rather than light, they hate the law and the commandments, they hate Christ.

sense.text: We got to come out of this state of loving darkness if we want to fix a broken people. The broken people are in darkness; the guide to fixing it is the light. The light got to come into the room, Christ got to come into the room, the Bible got to be open. “Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever”: he told Isaiah to write it down, and it’s happening in 2023.

“That this is a rebellious people”: our people are rebellious. How the hell we want to be fixed, but we rebellious? “Lying children”: we say we love the Lord, we go to church on Sunday, but believe in Groundhog Day. We think a damn groundhog can tell the Lord when to make it hot and when to make it cold, six more weeks of winter. Our people are damn crazy. “Children that will not hear the law of the Lord”: they hate the laws of the Lord, and they hate us when we come out there. But this is the guide to fixing our people; there’s only one guide, and that’s the Bible.

“Which say to the seers, See not”: they say to us, don’t come out here and call us crackheads, don’t call us weed heads, don’t call us prostitutes, don’t talk about my pastor; don’t see what we doing. “And to the prophets, Prophesy not unto us right things”: don’t tell us what the Bible say; close the Bible. “Speak unto us smooth things”: tell me everything gonna be all right. All you got to do is take your pocketbook out and shake it three times, and they don’t want no coins to fall out, they want that debit card; there’s an ATM in the front. Sow your seed and reap bountifully: give me three thousand dollars, you’ll get thirty thousand. Somebody’s still trying to get that thirty thousand, still in the trailer park, still living in their car. Our people are under a delusion, and the only way to fix this is to open the scriptures and go into the Bible.

Most preachers teach with their Bible closed. They’ll read one scripture, Jesus by the seaside, and then tell how they was on the railroad track among the rocks, and the Lord delivered them from smoking the wrong crack rock; the music starts playing and everybody jumps up and runs around the church. Then they take up an offering, go home, and come back and get high again next week. We got to come out of this stuff.

“Get you out of the way”: they say get out the block. The woman seen earlier said get them off the block, talking to the police, like we don’t have every right to be here just like her. “Turn aside out of the path, cause the Holy One of Israel to cease”: the Holy One of Israel is Christ, the light. They say cut the light back out; they want to remain in darkness and speak smooth words, but God got other plans.

A sister whose brother was shot robbing a Dollar General says the clerk shouldn’t have had a gun at work: that’s how crazy black people are, delusional; these are broken people talking. And this stuff goes on in the church: a man telling how a minister in the church who could sing and play the organ took advantage of him and opened his life up to homosexuality. That’s how they get you, if they can sing and play the organ. Christianity is the reason why people are broken, so to fix it you got to come out the Christian church. These homosexual spirits linger in the Christian church because they accept it, because they are of Satan; cross-dressing, all this stuff goes on in the Christian church. Satan is in there.

Let’s get to the solution. We go through all these things, but the Most High made a promise, and he’s going to keep his promise. We broke our promise, but the Most High gonna keep his.

“He cast upon them the fierceness of his anger”: he casts upon us the fierceness of his anger, “wrath, and indignation”: righteous anger; he rightfully done that. “And trouble”: this is what we’re living, this is what we’re seeing, this is why we was snared. “By sending evil angels among them”: God got evil angels, and he sends them among us when we are disobedient.

precepts.why:
“Yet they tempted and provoked the most high God, and kept not his testimonies”: that’s what we did; we made God angry and we did not keep his testimonies. To understand how to fix us, we got to understand what we’ve done. “But turned back, and dealt unfaithfully like their fathers”: like our forefathers.

“For they provoked him to anger with their high places”: we made God angry with our churches; that’s the high places. “And moved him to jealousy with their graven images”: we went into idolatry. “When God heard this, he was wroth, and greatly abhorred Israel”: when he got angry with us, he broke us.

sense.text: But God comes back and says “Fear not; for thou shalt not be ashamed: neither be thou confounded”: we won’t be confounded, “for thou shalt not be put to shame”: we’re not going to be put to shame forever. “For thou shalt forget the shame of thy youth”: the things we was doing in our past, the shame that we have caused upon us, we’re going to forget. “And shalt not remember the reproach”: the disappointment, “of thy widowhood any more”: we didn’t have a father.
“And thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel”: our Redeemer is going to be the Holy One of Israel, so salvation is coming. “The God of the whole earth shall he be called.”

“For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee.” He forsook us for a long time, but with great mercies he’s going to start to gather us, and he’s doing that now. All praise to the Most High, he’s using us to do these things. It’s not going to be like this all the time: Christ is on the way, our Redeemer is near, our salvation is near.

precepts.why:
“And now, O Lord God of Israel, that hast brought thy people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand”: he’s going to bring us out of Egypt with a mighty hand, “and high arm, and with signs, and with wonders”, which you can read about all through the Bible, “and with great power, and hast gotten thyself a name”: the Most High has gotten himself a name, meaning a reputation.

“O Lord our God, we have sinned, we have done ungodly, we have dealt unrighteously in all thine ordinances. Let thy wrath turn from us”: it’s a prayer. Lord, let your anger turn from us; let us repent. “For we are but a few left among the heathen, where thou hast scattered us. Hear our prayers, O Lord, and our petitions, and deliver us for thine own sake, and give us favour in the sight of them which have led us away: That all the earth may know that thou art the Lord our God, because Israel and his posterity is called by thy name.”

The Most High is going to wake us up, and we’re going to be for a sign that he is the only God that can take a people at such a low state and put them back together. But we got to follow the guide, what the Lord is requiring, for us to be put back together; we can’t keep doing our own thing. Right now we’re a broken people, but as our people wake up, and we go out to the streets or on social media sharing these videos and this truth throughout the earth, he’s fixing us one at a time, and it’s going to show his power throughout the earth.

He gonna make good his word. In order to fix a broken people you got to understand how he was broken, who was broken and why; that’s the only way it’s gonna get fixed. Until then we can stop complaining.

“If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy”: we got delivered to the enemy, “so that they carry them away captives”: we was carried away captive on cargo slave ships, “unto the land of the enemy”: we was brought here, to the land the conquistadors had already conquered, to the so-called white man, “far or near”.

“Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives”: King Solomon prayed, if we should remember who we are in this land, “and repent”: this is how it’s going to fix us. We got to repent and come back to the Lord. “Saying, We have sinned”: our people don’t even understand what sin is, so they can’t say we have sinned. They think not celebrating Christmas, not buying Christmas gifts for their kids, not going on the Easter egg hunt and painting the boiled eggs, is sin. “And have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”.

“And so return unto thee with all their heart”: we got to return unto the Lord with all our mind, meaning keeping the commandments, meditating day in and day out, “and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies”: right here in America, South America, Canada, Central America, China, wherever you may be. “And pray unto thee toward their land”: this is why we pray toward the east. We got to pray toward Jerusalem, not Mecca, because that is the land God chose, “which thou gavest unto their fathers, the city which thou hast chosen, and the house which I have built for thy name”.

If we want to fix our problem, we got to go to the book of the commandments; that’s the guide. “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever”: people tell y’all the laws of God are done away with, and that’s a lie. It endures forever, so the laws are still in existence. “All they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die”: you leave the Bible and say it’s done away with, and just want to go to church and jump around and hear some Yolanda Adams and some Kirk Franklin songs, you’re gonna continue to die.

“Turn thee, O Jacob”: Jacob is the twelve tribes of Israel, who were brought into captivity. “And take hold of it”: take hold of the Bible; that’s the guide that’s going to help us fix our problems. “Walk in the presence of the light thereof”: the light is Christ, the word of God, “that thou mayest be illuminated”: we’re going to be a light, the glow for the world.

“Give not thine honour to another”: to the heathens. This covenant is for us; stop trying to give it to other people. This is one reason why we can’t fix our problems: we think we can have other people among us and fix our problems, and they only come in to infiltrate and make sure you stay destroyed. “Nor the things that are profitable unto thee to a strange nation.”

“O Israel, happy are we”: we need to learn to be happy and stop complaining all the damn time, “for things that are pleasing to God are made known unto us”: the word of God, what’s pleasing to God, was made known unto us, not unto them; they know how to please the devil, the deceiver. “Be of good cheer, my people, the memorial of Israel”: the Most High has remembered us.

“Ye were sold to the nations, not for your destruction”: we were brought to America, “but because ye moved God to wrath”: because we made God angry. This is why we got here; we didn’t come to America to be equal to them or to live it up. “Ye were delivered unto the enemies”: delivered unto the so-called white man. “For ye provoked him that made you by sacrificing unto devils, and not to God”: we worshipped other gods and sacrificed to the deceivers of this world.

sense.text: “Behold, the Lord’s hand is not shortened, that it cannot save”: yes, we are broken, but the Lord’s hand is not shortened that he cannot deliver us. “Neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear”: he can hear us if we repent. He don’t want to hear us keep lying to him: Lord, I ain’t gonna get drunk no more, I ain’t gonna smoke no more rocks, I’m through sleeping around with Tyrone, I don’t want Keisha no more. The Lord don’t want to keep hearing that.

“But your iniquities have separated between you and your God”: this is why we cannot be fixed as a broken people, because of sin. Sin is separating us from being fixed. “And your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear”: so the Lord’s not hearing us.

“For your hands are defiled with blood”: our hands are defiled with blood, “and your fingers with iniquity”: our fingers are working iniquity. “Your lips have spoken lies”: our lips have spoken lies. “Your tongue hath muttered perverseness”: our tongue has muttered perverseness.

“None calleth for justice”: nobody’s calling for justice for us, “nor any pleadeth for truth: they trust in vanity”: we trust in the lies, in things that don’t matter, “and speak lies; they conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity”: that’s what we love to do.
